description: Zeck provider substitution map (Deployment & Runtime Architecture D1.0 sections 3 and 19). Zeck owns authority; providers implement operational ports. Every concern has an owning port, a reference provider and a documented replacement target. Failure behavior is explicit per dependency: the authoritative relational store fails closed; every non-authoritative dependency has an explicit degraded mode.

degradation.effect: Control-plane admission and every authority-bearing operation refuse. No datastore is silently promoted; no authority data exists outside PostgreSQL.
Operations requiring artifact bytes fail explicitly. Artifact metadata and provenance in PostgreSQL remain authoritative; no artifact bytes pass through PostgreSQL as a fallback.
Execution admission continues through PostgreSQL authority; dispatch is deferred and backlogged. A queued message is never mistaken for execution success; queue state is never an authority claim.
Waiting orchestrations pause; execution status, budget state, policy state and ledger state remain authoritative in PostgreSQL and resume on recovery.
Locks, rate limits and cache entries fall back to conservative local behavior. Redis holds no authority data, so its outage cannot corrupt or redefine durable application authority.

providers.commercialUse: Hobby-tier usage is permitted for personal/non-commercial development and preview only. Commercial production requires a commercially permitted plan; the API remains independently runnable so hosting can move without domain change.

degradation.effect: The experience layer is unreachable; control-plane and execution-plane authority are unaffected.
